body: While the Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane was fluffing his lines at one end of the pitch, Fabio Silva was preparing to rewrite the script at the other. His late equaliser for Borussia Dortmund in Der Klassiker must be the most important goal of his career.

It was magnificent too. The first touch was perfection to protect the ball and give him just enough space to arrow a shot into the far corner with his second. An 89th-minute equaliser away to Bayern Munich to maintain Dortmund's unbeaten record.

There is a feeling within Dortmund that he needed this as a reward for his efforts. Speaking to goalkeeper Gregor Kobel afterwards, he made the point that forwards need goals to feel good. Stealing the show from Kane could be a transformative moment.

Silva's potential has long been debated. He was just 18 when Wolves committed £30m to sign him from Porto, the club's chairman talking of a generational talent. items.excerpt: Arsenal won at Anfield for the first time in 14 years after Kai Havertz's strike sealed a gritty 1-0 victory - but Liverpool were denied what looked to be a clear penalty.
body: Arsenal won at Anfield for the first time in 14 years after Kai Havertz's strike sealed a gritty 1-0 victory - but Liverpool were denied what looked to be a clear penalty.
The result opens up a three-point gap on Manchester City at the top of the Premier League - and means Mikel Arteta's side are nine clear of Liverpool.

In a battle of attrition, the only discernible difference was at the top end. Liverpool's various waves of pressure almost always led to an effort on David Raya's goal - 17 in total - but none actually forced the goalkeeper into a save.

Florian Wirtz hit the crossbar with a free-kick and Alexis Mac Allister ballooned a header over the bar unmarked, but Andoni Iraola's side failed to land a single shot on target at home for the first time on record. "It's been a defensive masterclass from Arsenal," said Gary Neville.

body: Russo rescues point for Arsenal in frustrating afternoon vs Villa
Alessia Russo scored a late equaliser to salvage a 1-1 draw for Arsenal against Aston Villa as Renee Slegers' side failed to make their dominance count at the Emirates Stadium.

The Gunners had 27 shots in total at the Emirates but were left frustrated by a stoic defensive performance from Villa, who sat deep to preserve their lead after Chasity Grant scored with their only shot of the game in the 25th minute.
Villa defended valiantly, supported by eight saves from Akane Okuma, before Russo latched onto Stina Blackstenius' cross to head home the equaliser in the 85th minute.
